question: If the verified build were published into the branch root the way scripts/root_publish.py does it (fresh data files, frozen data/evidence), would the repository's own replay validator still accept the tree that checks.yml and pages.yml build from?
method: Materialised the data/ tree as it is committed at HEAD with `git archive HEAD data` into a temporary directory; the repository's own working tree was not modified. On a runner the working tree is NOT the checked-in fixture, because this workflow collects and originates live data before this step.
Simulation 1 overwrote exactly the data files scripts/root_publish.DATA_FILES would overwrite, from the newest saved live snapshot under data/research/*/live/, and left data/evidence/ frozen.

Simulation 2 ran scripts.root_publish.build_plan()/apply_plan() against a real built site/ tree, so the publisher itself decided what lands in the root, then replayed scripts.validate.check_data - the same call scripts.build makes first.
Both simulations report where their base tree came from, so a 'passed' result can never be mistaken for a measurement over an already-fresh tree.

traceback: require(request.get('status') == 'ok' and request.get('observed_at') == page['observed_at'], 'HLTV observation timestamp restamped')

conclusion: A root publish of a fresh snapshot would break the repository's own build: ValueError: HLTV observation timestamp restamped.
notes: Decisive measurement: simulation 2 (`scripts.root_publish`'s own plan over a build that was fresher than the committed root); simulation 1 measured a different, older candidate.
scripts.build calls scripts.validate.check_data first, so the build - and therefore checks.yml on every pull request and the pages.yml refresh - would fail on the published root.
The cause is the pairing root_publish.py documents: a fresh data/latest.json with the frozen data/evidence/ tree (its inventory observation timestamp no longer matches).

This is why the publisher shipped by this session re-deploys the verified artifact instead of committing fresh data to main: it makes the public site current without changing the frozen fixture that CI builds from.
34 checked-in test modules read data/latest.json or ROOT/'data' directly, so a committed fresh snapshot also moves their fixture underneath them.
